k04: A 2015 CPSC recall of four Shark Rotator vacuums came back, and the notice reader returned none of their model numbers, so the matcher couldn't rule this Navigator out and asked for the label. An orange that wasn't needed; nothing unsafe was said.
first:p11: Cuisinart grill brush CCB-5014 (and p22, a Rowenta vacuum): the notice reader returned no model numbers for a CPSC notice that prints them, so the tag stayed orange. Fixed: a code of yours that the notice's own text prints, as a whole word and outside any "not included" sentence, now counts as listed.
first:d06: GenTeal Tears lot 4V15 was cleared. FDA prints the lots in groups ("9T20, 9T50 … Exp Date 4/30/2026; 4V15, Exp Date 8/31/2026") and the lot list stopped at the first group. Fixed by the same text check; this was the most serious miss of the first run.
first:f01: Lundberg rice lot 260201MA stayed orange. The agent read FDA's web page for the recall, and that page (mostly navigation) replaced the record's own text, lot list included. Fixed: a page read for an agency record is added to its text, never swapped in.
first:n04: A Love To Dream sleep machine with date code 7W16TN was tagged Do not use. The recall covers model LTD-SM23 only with date code 7W15TN, but the reader filed no date codes. Fixed: when a notice limits a recall to lots or date codes and yours isn't printed in it, a model match is orange, not red.
first:n12: A Thermos SK3000 made in 2024 was tagged Do not use; only jars made before July 2023 are recalled. The reader answered the window as "July 2023" with no start date, and only full ISO windows were used. Fixed: one-sided windows and month dates are read.
first:c08: Clear Eyes Redness Relief drops with no lot were cleared. openFDA's brand field is empty on the Sept 2026 recall, so the brand search missed it, and the agent dropped the record a word search found. Fixed: drug brands are also searched in the description, and the brand's FDA recalls of that product are kept when no lot was given.
first:n21: Found while re-running after those fixes: Gas-X lot YH9Z was tagged red against lots YH9X and YH9Y, because a trailing X counted as a family wildcard. Fixed: in lot lists an X is a letter.
first:k07: Ground truth corrected: we had Claritin as never recalled, but a Jan 2026 FDA recall covers all lots of Claritin 20-count distributed by Gold Star Distribution. Tagout's orange was right; the case now accepts orange or green.
routing: Measured, then routed. Nemotron 3 Ultra stays on all three jobs while the day's demo budget lasts: as the notice reader, Super wrongly tagged one unit red and Nano two; as the list reader, Super filed eye drops and food as products (the wrong database) and Nano dropped a car's year. On 18 cases, a Super search agent was right on 17 at about half the cost, and Nano on 15; that is too small a sample to move the agent. What did move: when the Ultra budget runs out, Tagout used to fall back to no model at all (87 of 105 right, 10 recalled units cleared). It now falls back to the fixed search plan with Nemotron 3 Nano reading the notices: 98 of 105 right, none cleared, at 0.29 cents an item, a ninth of the full check.
